title: Chia Offer Builder
summary: How do you create an intuitive interface for a new way of trading digital assets?
alt: Offer Builder in the Seedling Wallet, with Offering and Requesting columns for XCH, tokens, NFTs, and fees.

sections.heading: Two interfaces, then NFTs
body: In the Chia Wallet, there were two different interfaces for offers — one for XCH trades and another for token trading. With NFTs soon to be added to the mix, neither of the existing interfaces would work. We needed an interface allowing any combination of assets to be traded for any other combination of assets that was also future-proof and intuitive to use.

sections.heading: A proposal, not a payment
body: I took a first principles approach with Offer Builder. Offers are different from transactions in that you are only creating a proposal for a transaction. This needs to be evident in the interface design. The solution we came up with needed to be intuitive, instructive, and durable.

frame.alt: Offer Builder in the Seedling Wallet, with Offering and Requesting columns for XCH, tokens, NFTs, and fees.

blocks.label: The challenge
blocks.text: We needed an interface allowing any combination of assets to be traded for any other combination of assets that was also future-proof and intuitive to use.

blocks.heading: A proposal, not a payment
body: In the Chia Wallet, there were two different interfaces for offers — one for XCH trades and another for token trading. With NFTs soon to be added to the mix, neither of the existing interfaces would work.

I took a first principles approach with Offer Builder. Offers are different from transactions in that you are only creating a proposal for a transaction. This needs to be evident in the interface design. The solution we came up with needed to be intuitive, instructive, and durable.

blocks.heading: The problem Chia Offers solves
body: Counterparty risk is a common concern in transactions, involving the potential for attackers to take your assets. Traditional finance relies on trusted intermediaries like escrow services, which hold assets until transaction conditions are met. However, on the internet, an attacker may also control the escrow service. This common attack leads to significant asset losses.

Blockchain, specifically the Chia blockchain, addresses this issue effectively. Using a UTXO-style architecture and aggregatable BLS signatures, Chia enables users to propose transactions ("Offers") that others can accept. The blockchain executes these zero-trust transactions, delivering assets to respective wallets. This allows individuals and institutions to conduct counterparty risk-free transactions.
Creating an offer as quickly as possible was my north star for this feature.

frame.alt: Early concept for NFT offers, with a dense token-style trading layout.
frame.caption: Early concepts for NFT offers were based on token trading interfaces and seemed overly complex. The established interface pattern broke when trying to trade multiple NFTs or groups of assets for groups of other assets.

frame.alt: Two-column offer concept, one side for assets you own and one for assets you want.
frame.caption: An offer sets the conditions for both sides of a transaction, so I chose to create two columns. One for items you own and want to trade, and another for items you would like to trade for.

frame.alt: Offer builder with XCH, tokens, and NFTs visible at the top level instead of inside a menu.
frame.caption: This new paradigm for trading is unfamiliar, so it’s essential we make the user think as little as possible. Hiding asset types under a dropdown menu might be more minimal looking, but it complicates the mental decision-making needed to create a trade. Placing all asset categories at the top level allows users to immediately see their options and construct an offer.

frame.alt: Offer Builder with an OR operator between two possible requested assets.
frame.caption: The Offer Builder interface allows for multiple assets to be traded and could include logic. In this case an OR operator (in black) could execute the trade if either of the conditions are met.

frame.alt: A wall of earlier offer interface iterations.
frame.caption: Offers went through dozens and dozens of iterations before we came to the conclusion that the current way of thinking about offers wouldn’t work with NFT or multi-asset offers.

frame.alt: Offer Builder with a seven-day expiration on the offer.
frame.caption: The most recent offers interface (as of Chia Wallet 2.1.1) allows offers to expire after a period of time.

frame.alt: The original offers interface beside the updated Offer Builder.
frame.caption: The original offers interface and the updated Offer Builder.

title: Chia Transaction Signer
summary: A better way to secure blockchain assets for enterprises and consumers.
alt: Chia Signer phone screens for keys, a signature request, QR codes, and the Secure Enclave.

sections.heading: Keys off the paper
body: Secure custody of digital assets is one of the biggest unsolved technology and UX problems in the blockchain space. Seed phrases are often misplaced, lost, or stolen by attackers. This leads to billions of dollars worth of crypto assets each year being stolen or lost. This kind of asymmetric risk is a major obstacle to adoption for average users and enterprises.

At Chia Network Inc., we approached this problem by separating the keys needed to sign and submit a transaction from the creation of a transaction. Securing the keys inside the Secure Enclave of an Apple device instead of on a piece of paper or metal presents a much better interface for securing and managing keys.

frame.alt: Chia Signer phone screens for keys, a signature request, QR codes, and the Secure Enclave.

blocks.heading: Keys off the paper
body: Seed phrases are often misplaced, lost, or stolen by attackers. This leads to billions of dollars worth of crypto assets each year being stolen or lost. This kind of asymmetric risk is a major obstacle to adoption for average users and enterprises.

At Chia Network Inc., we approached this problem by separating the keys needed to sign and submit a transaction from the creation of a transaction. Securing the keys inside the Secure Enclave of an Apple device instead of on a piece of paper or metal presents a much better interface for securing and managing keys.

Chia Signer is a mobile application specifically designed for the secure facilitation of blockchain transactions. The Chia blockchain enables the use of the Secure Enclave on Apple devices, making every iPhone a hardware wallet. With a much better interface, this application lets users sign, manage, and oversee blockchain transactions. It is designed to work with the Chia Vault and Chia Enterprise Wallet Service.
I created all of the UI/UX and branding elements for this project.

frame.caption: Users can see a list of keys and dive deeper into transactions with a key, as well as individual completed transactions.

frame.alt: Chia Signer scanning a QR code from an air-gapped machine to accept a spend request.
frame.caption: The most secure workflow allows users to accept spend requests from an air-gapped machine using QR codes.

title: Chia Reference Wallet
summary: A showcase of the feature primitives enabled by the Chia blockchain and Chialisp.
alt: Chia reference wallet on macOS, showing a token balance, a chart, and pending clawback transactions.

sections.heading: A reference, not a pitch
body: In order for developers to understand what is possible in a new programming environment and open-source blockchain ecosystem, there needs to be a reference implementation of features and primitives that developers can use as a guide in creating their own applications.

The Chia Reference Wallet is a reference implementation of almost all of the primitives on the Chia blockchain, including farming, plotting, pooling, tokens, Chia Offers, NFTs, verifiable credentials, decentralized identifiers, transaction clawback, contacts, and more. I worked on many of these features from zero to one, developing the UI and UX from scratch.

frame.alt: Chia reference wallet on macOS, showing a token balance, a chart, and pending clawback transactions.

blocks.heading: Already in the wallet
body: In the future, your crypto wallet will hold your identity, access to your certificates, diplomas, and other credentials, connect to your bank account, and hold any crypto assets you might have, including digital collectibles, tickets, securities, and investments.
The Chia Reference Wallet already has several of these advanced capabilities.
list: Offers. Zero-trust multi-asset trading between peers without marketplaces.
Asset undo. Set a time window to undo a transaction and claw back the funds.
Verifiable credentials. Unique on-chain assets that can verify data about a person without revealing their identity.
NFTs. Unique digital assets that can represent unique real-world assets or verifiably unique digital assets.
